name: mastodon-mcp
description: Mastodon (social): me, publish_text, read_comments, reply_comment, read_mentions, analytics_post, de

platform_mcp_mastodon_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_MASTODON_TOKEN
platform_mcp_mastodon_token.description: Mastodon user access token from the account's instance (Preferences > Development > New application, or an OAuth flow) with scopes read:accounts read:statuses read:notifications write:statuses; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

platform_mcp_mastodon_instance.title: PLATFORM_MCP_MASTODON_INSTANCE
platform_mcp_mastodon_instance.description: Host of the account's Mastodon instance without scheme, e.g. mastodon.social; every call goes to https://<instance>/api/v1/...

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials (user token, read:accounts) returns the CredentialAccount {id, username, acct, display_name, url, followers_count, ...}.

tools.name: publish_text
tools.description: POST /api/v1/statuses {status, in_reply_to_id} (write:statuses) returns the Status {id, uri, url, created_at, content, account}. Visibility, language, spoiler_text and scheduled_at keep the instance defaults; the Idempotency-Key header is not sent.

tools.name: read_comments
tools.description: GET /api/v1/statuses/:id/context returns {ancestors, descendants}; every descendant Status (HTML `content`) is returned in one response, so page/limit are not sent.

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: A reply is a status with in_reply_to_id set to the comment's status id.

tools.name: read_mentions
tools.description: GET /api/v1/notifications?types[]=mention (read:notifications); limit defaults to 40, max 80. Mastodon paginates with Link headers / max_id, so `page` is not sent: pass `since` (a notification id, sent as since_id) to read newer mentions. `text` is the mentioning status's HTML content.

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.description: GET /api/v1/statuses/:id returns the Status with replies_count, reblogs_count and favourites_count (https://docs.joinmastodon.org/entities/Status/); the runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: DELETE /api/v1/statuses/:id ('Delete one of your own statuses'; user token with write:statuses) returns 200 with the deleted Status carrying the source `text` (and poll / media_attachments) 'for reposting' - it is available under raw, and the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}. 401 'The access token is invalid' is an auth_error; 404 'Status is not owned by you or does not exist' is an invalid_input. DELETE statuses is rate limited at 30 per 30 minutes (https://docs.joinmastodon.org/api/rate-limits/).
